newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl meets Primakov to prepare Moscow trip.
newsitem.headline: Kohl meets Primakov to prepare Moscow trip.

text.p: German Chancellor Kohl held talks with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov on Thursday, two days before travelling to Moscow to see President Boris Yeltsin.

In discussions with his German counterpart Klaus Kinkel on Wednesday, Primakov committed Moscow to a dialogue with the West about Europe's new security architecture, but reiterated Russia's objections to an enlargement of NATO.

Neither Primakov nor Kohl commented to reporters on the content of their talks, but government spokesman Peter Hausmann said in a curt, six-line statement that the atmosphere had been "pleasant and friendly".

Germany is Russia's biggest aid-giver and, as Moscow's leading advocate in the West, spearheads efforts to bring Russia closer to international organisations such as the European Union and the NATO Western alliance.
Primakov's trip to Bonn was his first bilateral visit to any country in the West since he took office in January, and he praised the confidence he said existed between the countries.

Kinkel has said the visit marks the start of an intensive dialogue aimed at giving Russia a place in Europe's security architecture and formalising close relations with NATO before the alliance admits new members in eastern Europe.
Kohl visits Yeltsin on Saturday at a time of intense speculation about the health of the Russian leader, a subject which also figured in Primakov's talks with Kinkel.
Yeltsin has been seen in public only once since late June and declined to receive his security troubleshooter Alexander Lebed after he struck a peace deal with rebels in Chechnya.
Yeltsin's aides say he is in full control of policy but needs rest, and Bonn has played down Kohl's visit as an informal meeting with minimal protocol and no urgent agenda.
